subject: Sparse burst quota forecast and product clarifications for ClearPort launch
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@clearport.ai>, ops@clearport.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Sparse burst quota forecast and product clarifications for ClearPort launch

Samira / ClearPort team — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Per our call I want to capture the traffic shape and the asks so we can coordinate a temporary quota bump and product-level safeguards. Quick summary below and three asks for our product/infra teams.

Summary of expected pattern (per ClearPort model v2 attached):
- Baseline: ~15 requests/minute across the cluster during business hours.
- Peak burst: up to 9,000 requests over a 6–12 minute window triggered by user batch sync (estimated 60–75 concurrent sessions).
- Token profile: median 180 tokens per request, 95th percentile 520 tokens.
- Launch window: two-week marketing push starting Aug 4 (heavy bursts expected first 72 hours).

Immediate asks (what we need from Redwood):
1) Temporary quota increase: 3x baseline ingress and a burst token ceiling that accommodates the 9k short-window spike for the first 72 hours, then scale down to 1.5x for remainder of two-week window.
2) Graceful fallback policy: route non-essential sync requests to a distilled model variant (fewer tokens) during overload, with clear prioritization for sign-in / auth flows.
3) Warmup / cache priming: guidance from product/runtime on pre-warming KV caches and any required warmup traffic pattern to avoid cold-start token spikes.

Samira — if you can confirm the attached numbers are final (I flagged columns in the spreadsheet where estimates are fuzzy) we'll submit the quota request to infra and loop in the Console team for rollout windows.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
attach: clearport_sparseburst_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Samira Khan <samira@clearport.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@clearport.ai
Date: 2026-07-14T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Sparse burst quota forecast and product clarifications for ClearPort launch

Thanks Vivek — attaching a cleaned sheet and a short token sample file. A few clarifications inline:
- The 9k spike is our worst-case (marketing + scheduled sync overlap). Best estimate is 6k–8.5k depending on the email digest concurrency.
- We can mark non-critical syncs as "low-priority" (they retry after N seconds) — that should be fine for your fallback routing.
- Warmup: we can run a 30-minute warmup sequence that simulates the 75 concurrent sessions at 60rps spread across regions.

I'll leave the file versions with the numbered tabs: V2_clean.xlsx and token_profile_samples.txt.

Samira Khan
Head of Product, ClearPort AI
attach: V2_clean.xlsx, token_profile_samples.txt
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-14T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Sparse burst quota forecast and product clarifications for ClearPort launch

Looping infra & product questions into one thread. Quick tech readout from my side after scanning the attachments:
- Token distribution looks spiky but predictable. We'll need to bump allocated concurrent tokens for the ClearPort account to avoid hitting per-customer token ceilings.
- Two options for quota policy: 1) temporary quota uplift on hosted tier with automatic rollback after Aug 18, or 2) enable a short-term dedicated pool (reserved) for the first 72 hours. Dedicated gives stronger guarantees but requires a minimum commitment and a week lead time to provision.

Questions for product (Marissa / Grace):
- Can we implement an automatic soft-throttle that redirects low-priority syncs to the distilled model variant at 85% of account token usage? That would avoid hard 429s while preserving auth-critical flows.
- Any appetite to allow the customer to opt into a 30-minute scheduled warmup window (we could expose toggles in Console)?

If we go with option 1 (hosted uplift) I can file the quota ticket today; if option 2 we need approvals for a dedicated pool and the finance commit.

-- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Sparse burst quota forecast and product clarifications for ClearPort launch

Thanks — a couple of product considerations before we finalize the ask:
1) Soft-throttle policy: we can ship an account-level soft-throttle that reroutes to a lighter model at 80% of token budget. Implementation note: this requires a small Console change so customers can see the threshold and opt into auto-fallback. Timeline: 5 business days for a minimal Console flag and server-side gating.
2) Warmup API: exposing a scheduled warmup endpoint is reasonable but we should guard it behind rate-limited calls (single warmup per account per 24h) to prevent misuse. Implementation: 7–9 business days including testing.
3) Observability: we need to ensure ClearPort's telemetry (token-by-route) maps to our per-route dashboards. Karthik — can you validate their route naming?

Product ask to infra: If we provision a temporary hosted uplift, request: 3x request ingress + token cap to cover a 10-minute maximal window at 9k RPS equivalent. If they prefer burst-only capacity, we can configure a short-lived burst pool and a scheduled rollback.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Launch & Platform
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-16T17:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Sparse burst quota forecast and product clarifications for ClearPort launch

All — infra ops approved a hosted uplift path with guardrails. TL;DR: we can do the temporary uplift (option 1) with the following constraints and runbook.

Approved uplift parameters:
- Time window: Aug 4 00:00 UTC — Aug 18 23:59 UTC (72-hour elevated cap first 3 days)
- Ingress multiplier: 3x baseline for first 72 hours, then 1.5x for remainder
- Token ceiling: set per-account token ceiling to allow the 9k spike at 95th token percentile, with automated rollback triggers at 90% sustained utilization for >5 minutes
- Fallback: automatic soft-throttle to distilled model at 80% (as requested), low-priority syncs deprioritized by routing policy
- Warmup: we can accept a 30-minute scheduled warmup (ops will run the warmup job if ClearPort triggers it from Console)

Runbook highlights:
1) Pre-launch (J-7): finance approval for temporary usage costs and sign-off from ClearPort on warmup exact timing.
2) J-2: provisioning + smoke tests in staging using the provided warmup script. Karthik — please validate route names and hand over test payloads.
3) Launch day: on-call infra and product leads will be paged if 5min sustained utilization >90% or error rate >1.5%.
4) Rollback: automatic on Aug 19, manual rollback available earlier if agreed.

I'll file the uplift ticket and link the runbook to the HubSpot deal once we have finance sign-off. Vivek — please coordinate with Samira to lock warmup window and confirm the final attachment.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
